name: Yazid ibn Suhayb al-Faqir
nameAr: يزيد بن صهيب الكوفي، أبو عثمان، المعروف بالفقير

laqab.en: al-Faqir: so called because he complained of the vertebrae (faqar) of his back, not because he was poor

diedNote: The Taqrib gives no year. The Shamela record places his death between 101 and 110 AH; not verified in a primary source here.

taqrib.ar: المعروف بالفقير بفتح الفاء بعدها قاف، قيل له ذلك لأنه كان يشكو فقار ظهره، ثقة
taqrib.en: Known as al-Faqir, with fathah on the fa' then qaf, so called because he complained of the vertebrae of his back; reliable.

students.name: Abu Asim Muhammad ibn Abi Ayyub al-Thaqafi

verdicts.ar: هو يزيد بن صهيب، كوفي ثقة
verdicts.en: He is Yazid ibn Suhayb, a Kufan, reliable.

verdicts.ar: هو ابن صهيب يكنى أبا عثمان، تابعي مشهور، قيل له الفقير لأنه كان يشكو فقار ظهره ولم يكن فقيرا من المال
verdicts.en: He is Ibn Suhayb, kunya Abu Uthman, a well-known Successor; called al-Faqir because he complained of the vertebrae of his back, not because he lacked money.

flags.label: Misleading laqab
flags.detail: Al-Faqir looks like "the poor man" but refers to a back complaint (faqar al-zahr), as Ibn Hajar explains from the Muhkam: a man whose back vertebrae are broken is called faqir (Fath 1/436; Taqrib 7733).

flags.label: Former Kharijite view, recanted
flags.detail: The Shamela record notes that he held a Kharijite opinion and then abandoned it; the story is his own account in Sahih Muslim's hadith on intercession, where his meeting with Jabir changed his mind. Not re-verified against Muslim here.

flags.label: Identified in the isnad
flags.detail: Al-Bukhari (or his teacher) glosses the bare name in the chain of 335: "Yazid, that is Ibn Suhayb al-Faqir"; in 438 and 3122 he appears as Yazid al-Faqir.

bio: A Kufan Successor who heard Jabir ibn Abdullah, Ibn Umar and Abu Sa'id; his nickname al-Faqir has nothing to do with poverty and everything to do with a bad back. Few hadith are transmitted from him (Ibn Khirash: "his hadith scarce"), but the Jabir hadith of the five gifts passes through him to Sayyar and Hushaym in al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Nasa'i. Al-Tirmidhi alone of the six did not use him.

provenance.ref: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 4/418 and al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 9/272, as collected on the Shamela narrator record 7084
